content.intro: PHP runs in the PHP runtime and is often used to generate dynamic web responses and command-line output. In a normal web request, the browser receives the response, not the original PHP source. In this lesson, focus on basic programming concepts; then compare it with files, directories, and paths. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use prerequisites for learning php when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: PHP runs in the PHP runtime and is often used to generate dynamic web responses and command-line output. In a normal web request, the browser receives the response, not the original PHP source. For prerequisites for learning php, begin with basic programming concepts. Also distinguish files, directories, and paths; html fundamentals; basic http and networking concepts. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Prerequisites for Learning PHP
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for prerequisites for learning php from top to bottom. Start by identifying basic programming concepts, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
